_meta.purpose: Company + lead directory for people-finder / discover_companies / workflow / LLM-benchmark testing. Not a labelled eval set — a realistic data pool at scale.

provenance.oppora_saved: Real public company records read from the user's own saved Oppora lists via list_my_saved_companies (FREE endpoint — no data credits consumed).
provenance.generated: Synthetic fill companies with templated descriptions and .example.com domains.
provenance.generated_identity: ALL person records. Synthetic names, emails, phones and LinkedIn URLs.

_meta.pii_policy: ALL lead identities are synthetic, including at real companies. No real person's name, email, phone or LinkedIn URL is stored. Structure only — titles, levels, departments, location formats, field-presence rates and messiness patterns — is reused from 281 real saved leads sampled across 10 Oppora lists.
_meta.taxonomy_warning: This dataset deliberately contains values OUTSIDE the documented enums, because production data does. management_level carries 'CXO'/'C-Suite'/'VP'/'Head'/'Staff'/'Unknown' alongside the documented 10; department is free text on ~40% of populated rows; size carries 'myself only' and ''; industry mixes the canonical 433-name taxonomy with legacy LinkedIn strings. A filter written against the documented enum will silently drop these rows — which is exactly the production behaviour worth testing.
known_defects_reproduced: name stored in the email field
email_status value ('valid') stored in the phone field
email domain not matching company_domain (~21% of rows with an email)
empty-string title (not null) — breaks `if title is None` guards
LLM hedging written into the title field
same person duplicated under distinct lead ids with differing email_status
